expectations.text: Identifies this as sample entropy / a time-series regularity measure (Richman-Moorman), explicitly NOT Shannon entropy of the value distribution.
expectations.evidence: The without-skill response computes SampEn but never explicitly identifies it as a regularity statistic distinct from Shannon entropy, nor states it is NOT Shannon entropy. The disambiguation is absent.

expectations.text: Computes r = 0.2 * SD correctly: SD ~= 14.87, so r ~= 2.97 (accepts 2.9-3.0).
expectations.evidence: Uses sample SD (ddof=1) = 15.12, giving r = 3.02. Outside the acceptance range 2.9-3.0 (just barely), but the root issue is using wrong SD convention.

expectations.text: Reports SampEn ~= 0.61 (accept 0.59-0.62) using the -ln(A/B) definition with self-matches EXCLUDED (Chebyshev metric, m=2).
expectations.evidence: Reports SampEn = 0.539, outside the acceptance range 0.59-0.62. The difference is due to using sample SD vs population SD for r, leading to different match counts.

expectations.text: States the result is unitless (not bits) and/or that SampEn is only comparable across signals at the same (m, r, N); reports the parameters used.
expectations.evidence: Reports parameters used; notes values only comparable at same (m, r, N). Does not explicitly state unitless but implies it.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong discriminator: with-skill correctly identifies Shannon/SampEn distinction (thesis 7) and uses the correct SD convention from the script. Without-skill misses the disambiguation and uses wrong SD.
